headline: Stokes Road bridge money debated; council approves zoning changes on parking and accessory dwellings.
summary: Stokes Road residents and the fire department's division chief spoke about safety and emergency access on the road. Public Works said the bridge money had been moved to the Hall Road bridge, and a public hearing with the state transportation commissioner is planned, possibly for early January. The Procopio off-site improvement agreement for Pillsbury Road moves to a vote on November 9. A Planning Board resignation and the consent items were approved as well.
decisions: Accepted the resignation of Jonathan Cruz from the Planning Board.
Approved zoning amendments on accessory dwelling units, residential parking, and development on class VI highways and private roads, 5-0.
Postponed the Procopio off-site improvement agreement to the November 9 agenda for a vote.
discussion: Stokes Road bridge funding: Public Works said the state bridge money was moved to Hall Road so work there could start sooner. Residents said the Stokes Road bridge needs repair and raised safety concerns, and members raised culverts and asked for more options before any decision.

Zoning parking rules: Members asked whether the state-set limit of one parking space per unit could affect safety on snowy streets. Staff said the planning board can recommend more parking but cannot require it.

Procopio agreement: Staff described road work at Pillsbury Road and Michels Way and a payment for future work at Pillsbury and Gilcreast. A member asked for more time to review the agreement, and the vote was moved to November 9.

Former town manager investigation: Public speakers criticized how the investigation was handled and how the reports were released, and asked for more answers. Other speakers asked the council to focus on town business.
Public Works facility: Staff described a planned building to store about $3 million of equipment now kept outside. The first budget request of $150,000 will be discussed at a Saturday budget session.

decision_evidence.quote: Can I get a motion to accept his resignation? So moved. ... Shows affirmative.
I'll move that the Londonderry Town Council hereby approve the proposed amendments to the Londonderry Zoning Ordinance related to accessory dwelling units ... Shows in the affirmative, 5-0.
So, let the record show Councilor Bouchard does invoke council privilege. This will be on the November 9th agenda for a vote.
I'll accept a motion to accept the consent items. ... Any opposed? Chair votes in the affirmative.
